transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well… I suppose I’m here because things at home have gotten hard to ignore, and my wife thinks I’m reading too much into it, but I don’t think it’s just nothing.

It’s been going on for about a year, maybe a little more depending on where you start counting. She’s had these late meetings at work, and I understand people have late meetings — I’m not unreasonable about that — but it’s the way they happen, the timing, and then the little changes in her work messages. Like wording that shifts slightly, or things that are sent at odd times, or a phrase that seems out of place. She says it’s just office stuff, scheduling, people being busy, whatever. But when you see the same kinds of things line up again and again, it starts to feel too precise to be accidental.

I know how that might sound. I teach, I’m around students and faculty, I know people can overinterpret patterns. But this doesn’t feel like random insecurity to me. It feels like there’s a private signal in it, like something is being communicated indirectly — something she won’t just come out and say to me. And I’ve been trying to make sense of it, probably talking about it too much at home, because it’s creating tension. So… that’s why I’m here.
Do you believe your wife is actually sending you hidden messages through her work communications?

Yes… I mean, I wouldn’t say she’s literally writing “messages” to me in the obvious sense. That’s what makes it difficult to explain without sounding like I’m forcing it. But yes, I do think there’s something in those communications that’s meant to point to something she isn’t saying directly.

She keeps saying the late meetings are just late meetings, and the wording in the work messages is just normal office wording, people rushing, people changing schedules, that sort of thing. And I understand that can happen. I really do. But over the past year, these things have lined up in ways that feel too exact to be accidental — the timing, a phrase appearing right after something we talked about at home, a small change in how something is written, messages coming at odd times. Individually, maybe you could explain each one away. But all together, it feels like a private signal, like there’s meaning underneath it.

So yes… I believe she’s communicating something indirectly. I don’t think she’s willing to just say it plainly to me, and that’s why it keeps coming through in these small ways.
Do you think your wife's supposed hidden messages are meant for you alone, or could someone else also understand what she's trying to communicate?

I think… mostly for me. That’s the part that’s hard to explain, because if I showed the messages to someone else, they’d probably say, “This is just a scheduling email,” or “This is normal work chatter.” And on the surface, yes, I can see that. I’m not saying every person who reads it would immediately know what it means.

But the meaning seems tied to things only I would notice — the timing, the way a phrase comes right after something we talked about at home, little changes in wording, late meetings lining up in a way that feels too precise. Someone else might not have the context. They wouldn’t know what had been said between us or how unusual certain things are for her.

So no, I don’t think it’s some public code that everyone can understand. It feels more like a private signal meant for me, meant to tell me something she won’t say directly. That’s why it bothers me so much, because it’s not obvious enough that I can point to one line and prove it, but it’s consistent enough that I can’t just dismiss it as ordinary office stuff either.
Do you think your wife would admit to sending you these hidden messages if you confronted her about it?

No… I don’t think she would admit it. She hasn’t so far, really. When I bring it up, she says the late meetings are just work and the messages are just normal office stuff, and she makes it sound like I’m taking ordinary things and making them into something else.

But that’s exactly the problem — if she were willing to say it directly, then there wouldn’t be this whole pattern in the first place. The changes in wording, the timing, the way something shows up right after we’ve had a conversation at home… those things have been lining up for about a year now in a way that feels too precise to be accidental. So if I confronted her and said, “Are you sending me some kind of private signal?” I’m pretty sure she’d deny it.

And I understand how that sounds. I know she could say, “You’re imagining it,” or “That’s just a work message.” But to me it feels like there’s something underneath it, something she won’t just say plainly. So no, I don’t think she’d admit it — not unless she was ready to tell me what it actually means.
Have you ever considered the possibility that your interpretations of your wife's messages might be incorrect?

I have considered it, yes. I don’t want to come across like I’ve never asked myself that, because I have. I’ve sat there and thought, “Maybe this is just me reading too much into it. Maybe late meetings really are just late meetings, and maybe the wording in the messages is just normal office wording.” I know that’s what she says, and I understand that, in ordinary circumstances, that would be the simplest explanation.

But then I come back to the pattern. It’s not one message, or one late night, or one phrase that seemed odd. It’s been going on for about a year, and the timing of things, the little changes in how something is written, the way something shows up right after something we talked about at home — it all lines up too precisely for me to feel comfortable calling it accidental.

So yes, I’ve considered that I could be wrong. I’m not trying to be unreasonable. But when I look at the whole picture, it still feels like there’s a private signal in it, like she’s trying to tell me something indirectly that she won’t say out loud. That’s the part I can’t just set aside.
Has your belief that your wife is sending you hidden messages been causing you a lot of stress or affecting your daily activities?

Yes, it has caused stress, mostly at home. I wouldn’t say my whole life has fallen apart or that I can’t function, because I’m still going to work, I’m still doing my usual things, taking care of myself, keeping up with routines. At work I haven’t had any major problems from it.

But in my marriage, yes, it’s been a lot. We’ve had repeated tense conversations about it, and they tend to go in circles — I ask about the messages or the timing, she says I’m misreading things, and then I feel like she’s avoiding what’s really going on. It’s exhausting for both of us.

We were seeing a couples therapist, and eventually the therapist suggested that I get an individual assessment, which honestly made me feel a bit singled out at first. But I also understand that the situation has gotten tense enough that it probably needs to be looked at separately. So, yes, it’s affecting my daily life mainly through the strain in my marriage, not so much through work or basic routines.
Do you ever have moments where you doubt your interpretation of these messages and consider that they might just be ordinary communications?

Yes, I do have moments like that. I mean, I’m not completely closed off to the idea that they could be ordinary communications. I know my wife says the late meetings are just work, and that the little changes in wording in her messages are just normal office stuff. And sometimes I do sit there and think, all right, maybe I’m making too much of it, maybe if someone else looked at the same thing they wouldn’t see anything unusual.

But then I start thinking through the timing again, and the way certain phrases show up, or the way something seems to shift right after we’ve talked about something at home, and it’s hard for me to just dismiss that. It’s been going on for about a year, and it doesn’t feel like one random misunderstanding. It feels too precise, like there’s some private signal in it, like she’s trying to tell me something without saying it directly.

So yes, there are moments of doubt. I can say that honestly. But the doubt doesn’t really last, because when I look at the whole pattern, it still feels like there’s something underneath the ordinary explanation.
Do you think it's possible that you might be wrong about your wife sending you hidden messages?

I think it’s possible in the abstract, yes. I mean, I can say the words, “Maybe I’m wrong,” and I do try to think that through because I don’t want to be unfair to her or make something out of nothing.

But when I look at what’s actually been happening over the past year, it’s hard for me to believe it’s all just ordinary work communication. She says the late meetings are just late meetings, and that the little changes in wording in her messages are just normal office stuff, and I understand that explanation. I really do.

It’s just that the timing of things lines up too precisely. A phrase will shift after something we’ve talked about at home, or a message will come in a way that feels like it’s referring to something without saying it openly. If it happened once or twice, I could probably let it go. But over and over, it starts to feel like a pattern, like there’s a private signal in it meant for me, like she’s trying to tell me something she won’t say directly.

So… yes, I suppose I might be wrong. But honestly, it doesn’t feel wrong to me when I put all the pieces together.
Do you think you could ever be convinced that your wife's messages are just ordinary communications without any hidden meaning?

I suppose I could be convinced, but it would take a lot, because right now it doesn’t feel like just ordinary communication to me.

I know what my wife says. She says the late meetings are late meetings, and the changes in wording in her work messages are just normal office things — schedules shifting, people phrasing things differently, that sort of thing. And I understand that, logically. I’m not saying I can’t hear that explanation.

But the problem is that for the past year, the timing has felt too exact. It’s not just one message where I thought, “Oh, that’s odd.” It’s the way certain things seem to line up, like something will be said at home, and then later there’s a phrase or a change in wording that feels connected to it. It feels like there’s a private signal in there, like she’s trying to tell me something without actually saying it directly.

So could I ever be convinced? Maybe, yes, if there were some way to really show me that all of those patterns were accidental. But just being told “it’s normal office stuff” hasn’t been enough, because when I look at the whole thing together, it still feels like there’s meaning underneath it.
Do you think other people would understand the hidden meaning in your wife's messages if you explained it to them?

I think… some people might, if I explained the whole context carefully. Not if they just glanced at one message by itself, because then I know it could look ordinary. A late meeting on a calendar, a slightly different phrase in a work text, a change in wording — by themselves, those things don’t necessarily prove anything. I understand that.

But if I sat someone down and walked them through the timing, the sequence of it, the way certain things have lined up over the past year, then I think at least some people would see why it feels like more than coincidence. It’s not just that she has late meetings. It’s that they happen in a way that seems connected to other things. And it’s not just that her messages have small wording changes, it’s that the changes sometimes seem to come right after something has been said at home, almost like there’s a private signal in them.

My wife says it’s normal office stuff, and I know other people might start from that explanation too. I’m aware of that. But if they really listened and didn’t just dismiss me right away, I think they’d understand why I can’t just shrug it off. Whether they’d agree completely, I don’t know. But I think they’d see what I’m seeing, or at least see why I think there’s something she’s trying to tell me without saying it directly.
Have you been acting differently towards your wife because of your belief that she's sending you hidden messages?

Yes… I have, I suppose. I don’t like admitting that, because I don’t think I’ve been trying to punish her or anything like that, but it has changed the way things are between us.

Mostly it comes out at home. I ask more questions than I used to, and then she gets defensive, and then I feel like she’s avoiding the real issue, and it turns into another tense conversation. Sometimes I’ll bring up a message or a meeting or some wording that seemed strange to me, and she’ll say I’m reading into it, and then we go around and around. It’s been hard on the marriage, honestly.

It got to the point in couples therapy where the therapist suggested that I should maybe have an individual assessment too, not just keep trying to handle it as a couples issue. That was difficult to hear, because from my side it feels like I’m responding to something that’s really happening, not just creating conflict out of nowhere.

But outside of that, I wouldn’t say my life has fallen apart. I’m still going to work, doing what I need to do there. I’m keeping up with my usual routines, taking care of myself, that kind of thing. It’s really the marriage where it’s showing up the most — the repeated arguments, the tension, the feeling that we can’t have a normal conversation about it without it becoming charged.
Do you think there's anything your wife could say or do that would make you completely stop believing she's sending you hidden messages?

Completely stop? I don’t know. That’s the hard part, because if she just says, “There’s nothing there, they’re normal work messages,” that doesn’t really settle it for me anymore. I know that’s what she says — the late meetings are just late meetings, the little changes in wording are just normal office stuff. And I do understand that those things can happen in any job.

But after a year of noticing it, it feels like it’s not just one or two odd things. It’s the way they line up. The timing feels too precise to be accidental sometimes, like there’s a private signal in the way things are worded or when they happen, like she’s trying to tell me something without saying it straight out.

So if you’re asking whether she could say one thing that would make me completely drop it, probably not. Maybe if there were some way to go back and explain every instance, every timing, every phrase that stood out to me, and have it all make sense as coincidence or office routine, maybe that would help. But just reassurance from her hasn’t been enough, because part of me feels like if there is a hidden meaning, then of course she wouldn’t say it directly. That’s what makes it so difficult.
Would finding an alternative, plausible explanation for the patterns you've noticed in your wife's messages change your belief that they contain hidden meanings?

It might… I mean, I want to say yes, because I don’t want to be unreasonable about it. If there were an explanation that really accounted for the patterns, not just one message at a time, then I’d have to think about it seriously.

But the difficulty is that my wife has already said the late meetings and the little changes in her work messages are just normal office things, and I do understand that on a basic level. People have late meetings. People write things slightly differently depending on the day. I’m not saying every single odd wording means something by itself.

It’s more that, over the past year, they’ve lined up in a way that feels too precise to be accidental. The timing, the changes in phrasing, when they happen after certain things… it feels like there’s a private signal in them, like she’s trying to tell me something she won’t say directly.

So if someone gave me an alternative explanation that explained the whole pattern, not just brushed off each piece separately, maybe it would loosen my belief. But it would have to really fit what I’ve been seeing. Just saying “that’s normal office stuff” probably wouldn’t be enough, because that’s what I’ve been trying to accept, and it still doesn’t explain why it feels so deliberate to me.
Do you think your belief in the hidden messages would change if your wife were to leave you or pass away?

I… honestly, I don’t know that it would just disappear. That’s a strange question to think about, and I don’t like thinking about either of those things happening, obviously. But if you’re asking whether the belief is only there because she’s physically present to keep doing it, I’m not sure it works that simply in my mind.

Part of me would think, well, if she left, maybe that would be the message finally becoming direct in a way — like all the things I’ve been noticing were leading up to something she wouldn’t say plainly. And if she were gone, I suppose I might still look back at the messages and the timing and think, “No, there was something there.” Because it’s not only about what she says to me now. It’s that for the past year these late meetings and the small changes in wording in her work messages have lined up in ways that feel too exact to just be random office routines.

I know she says it’s normal work stuff. I hear that. But it feels like there’s been a private signal in it, something meant for me to understand without her saying it outright. So if she left or… passed away, I don’t think that would automatically make me say, “Oh, none of that meant anything.” I might not know what to do with it, but I think I’d still feel like the pattern had been real.
Do you think your belief in the hidden messages would still be present if you were to receive a direct and honest explanation from your wife about her communications?

If she sat down and was really direct and honest with me, I’d listen. I don’t want to make it sound like I wouldn’t hear her at all. Part of me wants exactly that — for her to just explain everything plainly so I can stop turning it over in my head.

But I have to be honest, I don’t know that it would fully go away just because she explained it. She has already told me the late meetings are just late meetings, and that the little changes in wording in her work messages are just normal office things. And I understand that, intellectually. I mean, I know people’s schedules change, people phrase things differently, work gets busy.

The problem is that over the past year, it hasn’t felt like isolated things. It’s the way they line up — the timing, the wording, when certain messages come through. It feels too precise to be accidental sometimes, like there’s a private signal in there, something meant for me to pick up on, something she won’t say directly.

So if she gave me a direct explanation, maybe it would help, depending on how much it actually accounted for. But if it was just, “No, you’re wrong, it’s normal work communication,” I don’t think that would completely settle it for me. I’d probably still be thinking, “But why did it happen that way, at that time, with those words?” That’s the part I can’t seem to let go of.
Do you think your belief in the hidden messages would still be present even if all evidence and explanations pointed to them being just ordinary communications?

I think… I think some part of it would probably still be there, yes. I know that may sound like I’m not being fair to the evidence, but that’s honestly where I get stuck.

Because I do hear the ordinary explanations. I know my wife says the late meetings are just late meetings, and the changes in wording in her work messages are normal office stuff. And if you laid it all out on paper, maybe it would look perfectly reasonable — schedules change, people send messages quickly, wording shifts depending on stress or workload or who they’re responding to.

But for me it’s not just one thing. It’s been this whole pattern over the past year, the way the timing and the phrasing seem to line up too precisely. That’s the part that makes it hard for me to let go of. It feels like there’s something in them meant for me to notice, like a private signal, like she’s trying to tell me something she won’t say directly.

So even if all the explanations pointed toward them being ordinary communications, I’m afraid I might still be thinking, “Yes, but what about the way it all fits together?” I don’t want to be stubborn. I really don’t. But the feeling that it’s deliberate has been very hard to shake.
Do you think your belief in the hidden messages would still be present even if your wife provided a detailed, logical explanation for each of the incidents you've interpreted as messages?

I think it would help, maybe, if she really went through each thing carefully. I don’t want to pretend that wouldn’t matter. If she could say, “This meeting ran late because of this,” or “I used that wording because of this email thread,” then yes, I’d try to take that seriously.

But if you’re asking whether it would make the belief completely vanish… I’m not sure. Probably not completely. Because the hard part for me isn’t just one incident where I misunderstood a sentence. It’s that, for about a year now, these things have seemed to line up in a way that feels too exact. The late meetings, the little changes in how she phrases work messages, the timing of when they happen — it feels like more than ordinary office noise.

So even if she gave me a logical explanation for each one, I think I might still be left with this feeling of, “Yes, but why did all of them fit together like that?” That’s the part I can’t quite get past. I know she says it’s normal work stuff. I understand the explanation when I hear it. But emotionally, or instinctively, it still feels like there’s a private signal in there meant for me, like she’s trying to tell me something without saying it directly.
Do you think your belief in the hidden messages would still be present even if everyone around you, including your wife and professionals, told you that there was no hidden meaning?

Yes… I think it probably would still be there, at least partly. I don’t like saying that, because it makes me sound like I’m just refusing to listen to anyone, and I don’t feel like that’s what I’m doing. If my wife told me there was nothing hidden, and you told me that, and other professionals or people around me all said the same thing, I would hear it. I would try to take it in.

But the problem is that it’s been going on in my mind for about a year now, and it doesn’t feel like just one misunderstanding that someone can explain away. It’s the pattern of it. The late meetings, the little changes in the wording of her work messages, the timing of when certain things happen — I know she says it’s all normal office stuff, and maybe everyone else would see it that way too. I can understand that on one level.

But it still feels too precise to me. Like there’s something in the way it lines up that isn’t accidental. Like there’s a private signal in it, something meant for me to notice, something she won’t say directly. So even if everyone said, “No, there’s no hidden meaning,” I think I’d still be left with that nagging thought of, “But then why does it fit together like that?” That’s the part that doesn’t go away easily.
Do you think your belief in the hidden messages would still be present even if you were shown clear evidence that disproved their existence?

I think… if it was really clear evidence, I would want to say no, that it would stop. That’s the reasonable answer, isn’t it? If something is disproved, then you let it go.

But honestly, I’m not sure it would disappear completely for me. It might weaken it. I might feel embarrassed, even, and try to tell myself, “All right, this proves it wasn’t what you thought.” But there’s still this part of me that keeps coming back to the pattern.

Because my wife has said the late meetings are just late meetings, and the small changes in her work messages are just normal work things, and I do understand that when she says it. I’m not saying every single thing on its own is impossible to explain. It’s more that, over the past year, the timing and the wording and the way these things seem to happen together have felt too precise to be accidental.

So even if you showed me clear evidence that there weren’t hidden messages, I think I might still have this nagging feeling afterward, like, “But why did it line up that way?” That’s where I get stuck. It feels like there’s some private signal in them, something meant for me to notice, like she’s trying to tell me something she won’t say directly. I know that may not sound logical, especially if there’s evidence against it, but the feeling has been very hard for me to shake.
Do you think your belief in the hidden messages would still be present even if you were shown clear, undeniable proof that they don't exist?

If you mean truly undeniable proof… I’d like to think I would accept it. I mean, I’m not trying to be unreasonable. I know there’s a part of this that sounds like I’m holding onto something even when other explanations are available, and that bothers me.

But if I’m being completely honest, I don’t know that the feeling would be gone right away. It might be weakened, maybe a lot. I might tell myself, “Okay, that proves there wasn’t anything there.” But I think some part of me would still keep circling back to how it’s all lined up over this past year.

Because my wife says the late meetings are just late meetings, and that the little changes in her work messages are just normal office things — different wording, timing, whatever was happening at work. I can understand that when she explains it. But to me, the timing and the wording have felt too exact, too connected, like there’s a private signal in there meant for me, like she’s trying to tell me something she won’t say directly.

So even with proof, I think I’d probably still have this… residue of doubt, I guess. Not as strong maybe, but still there, asking why it all fit together so neatly if there was nothing behind it.
